chunks: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the minimum of what occurs from the menstruation (haydh). So he said: Three (days), and its maximum is ten (days).

key_terms.أدنى: Minimum, least amount; used here as a legal term for the minimum duration
key_terms.الحيض: Haydh — menstruation; the natural blood discharge that triggers a series of jurisprudential rulings regarding purity, prayer, fasting, and marital relations
key_terms.ثلاثة: Three — the minimum number of days of menstruation recognized as legally valid haydh
key_terms.عشرة: Ten — the maximum number of days of menstruation

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum and maximum duration of menstruation (haydh) according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr reports asking Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) about the minimum duration of menstruation. The Imam ruled that the minimum is three days and the maximum is ten days — a ruling of fundamental importance in Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh) regarding ritual purity (taharah), prayer, and fasting obligations for women.
